To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quaternary states are not as rigid as was previously thought, that the Bohr effect is more complicated than originally thought, that the structure is more open in the B state of Tibetan snow leopard hemoglobin, that the structure of equine R-state CNmetHb is similar to the T state of human deoxyHb, and that the mass spectrometry of cyanomethhemoglobin can be used to help resolve the sequence of hemoglobins.

1) the quaternary structure of vertebrate hemoglobin is a dynamic process that is sensitive to pH and oxygenation state; 2) the quaternaries of the vertebrate hemoglobbins are different in the T and R states and are different for the different vertebrates; 3) these changes are important for the Bohr-effect and for the function of hemoglobin; 4) the quaternay structure is also different in the presence and absence of the ligand CN

the combination of neutron and X-ray crystallography with mass spectrometric analysis of hemoglobin is providing novel insights into the structural and functional changes in the protein between the different quartenary states of the molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the quaternary structural differences between the T and the R state and the proton changes that accompany this change in structure.
elucidating the structural changes that occur in hemoglobin between the R and T state and how this affects the protein's function.
the structure of the vertebrate hemoglobin molecule and the relationship of structure to function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bohr effect is not a simple protonation/deprotonation process, but a more subtle and complex process involving protonation/deprotection and solvent rearrangement.
hemoglobin structure and function is still a work in progress.
hemoglobin is a complex protein with a rich structural chemistry and biology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quaternary structure of vertebrate hemoglobin is more dynamic than previously thought, with the possibility that the T and R states are in equilibrium.
we are using the latest neutron diffraction techniques to examine the structural changes that occur in hemoglobin as the protein switches from the T to R state.

the combination of neutron diffraction, X-ray crystallography and mass spectrometry provides a unique opportunity to interrogate the structural and dynamic properties of the hemoglobin quaternary states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
combining neutron, X-ray, and mass spectrometry techniques is a powerful tool for the analysis of protein structure and function.
neutron and mass spectrometry studies of hemoglobin are providing additional insights into the quaternary structural states of the protein and their role in erythrocyte physiology.

the combination of neutron diffraction, X-ray diffraction, and mass spectrometry can help to resolve structural ambiguities in proteins of known sequence and to provide structural information in the case of proteins of unknown primary sequence.
